newsitem.title: CHINA: China futures slump may shut 100 brokerages.
newsitem.headline: China futures slump may shut 100 brokerages.

text.p: China's slumping futures market could see the closure of several exchanges and force up to 100 of the country's 300 futures brokerages to shut their doors by the end of 1997, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

China's futures market has been crippled by a government crackdown on speculation in the past three years and greater investor interest in the soaring stock market, the newspaper said, quoting Gao Aiguo, an analyst at Jinpeng International Futures Co in Beijing.
Although industry analysts had predicted an upturn in the futures market this year, liquidity has dried up on China's 14 commodities futures exchanges and market sentiment is weak, Gao said.

In the first five months of 1997, the total transaction volume of the futures market fell 30 percent from the same period last year, he said, but gave no figures. Only five of China's 14 futures exchanges have active trading, Gao said.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission, the market watchdog, has tried to stop futures speculation by suspending some contracts and introducing new penalties for misconduct, the newspaper said.
China could shut all but four or five of the country's futures exchanges and reduce the number of futures brokerages to 100, the newspaper said.
China's 14 futures exchanges trade mainly agricultural commodities and nonferrous metals.
